newsitem.title: GERMANY: De Silguy hopeful for stability pact before yr-end.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy hopeful for stability pact before yr-end.

text.p: European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday he hoped full agreement could be reached by the end of the year on a stability pact for the single European currency.

Replying to reporters' questions after a speech to the Franco-German Society in Frankfurt, De Silguy said: "There is no huge discussion of this in the Council of Ministers. I hope it will be possible to have agreement by the end of the year."
A stability pact is to be put in place to enforce sustained budgetary rigour among governments taking part in European economic and monetary union (EMU).
De Silguy nonetheless acknowledged that there was still disagreement on the circumstances under which a country could be exempted from sanctions under a stability pact.

"This (the exceptions) is really the only point which is now open. When you consider a year ago when (German Finance Minister) Mr (Theo) Waigel suggested the pact, it was like a bomb. Now it is amazing the consensus there is."

De Silguy said that while the Commission itself was reluctant to precisely define the circumstances which would allow a country to avoid sanctions, "if there is a political will to quantify this, we are ready to work on that."
De Silguy also sought to clarify a controversial decision by the EU last week to allow France to include a 37.5 billion French franc ($7.3 billion) transfer from France Telecom to state finances.

"(That) is not a judgement on France's ability to achieve sustainable convergence," he said, adding that such "one shot stuff" did not offer proof of a country's ability to sustain the Maastricht criteria for EMU entry.

The EU is due to deliver an initial report on which countries should form part of EMU by the end of next year, ahead of a special summit set for early 1998 to decide which countries will be eligible to join the single currency in 1999. ($1=5.120 French Franc)
